Always among the best modern-style Pinotages in the country, this is an equal blend of grapes from the Paardeberg and Malmesbury, marrying decomposed granite and ferricrete soils. Fermented with 15% whole bunches and aged in older oak, it’s a floral, engaging, selfassured style with detailed, finely judged tannins, layers of raspberry, redcurrant and fennel and a rose petal top note.

Blended from two sites in the Swartland, one on iron-rich soils in Malmesbury, the other on the schist of the Riebeekberg, this is a compact, appropriately ferrous Syrah that was fermented with 100% whole bunches. Left on skins for three weeks, it’s an intense, peppery, almost peaty style, with layers of kelp, green malt, blackberry and steak tartare and a firm, age-worthy finish.

n: Zandvliet Hill of Enon Small Berry Pick Shiraz
d: Hill of Enon comes from a small, 0.9-hectare parcel and is the stand-out Syrah in Robertson. It’s a finely judged, medium-bodied style that will delight northern Rhône Valley aficionados, with some clove and tobacco leaf notes from 30% whole bunches, bramble, blackberry and liquorice flavours and a waft of oak spices from older French and American barrels.

Kalkveld uses grapes from a single, 29-year-old parcel on limestone rich soils. It’s a very stylish expression of Syrah from the talented Jacques Cilliers with violet and fynbos aromas, layers of bramble, summer berries and white pepper and deftly integrated 30% new oak.

Jacques Cilliers blends Syrah with 13% Grenache and 11% each of Carignan and Mourvèdre to produce this well-priced, foudre-aged red. Clove, pepper and fynbos aromas are a scented introduction to a palate of bramble and sweet red berries complemented by fine-grained tannins.

Jacques Cilliers makes some of the best-value Syrahs, or Shirazes, in the Cape, typified by the quality of this wine from Robertson. Forward, textured and appealing, it has layers of clove, pepper and rooibos tea, fine tannins, a dab of oak and a core of bramble and red berry fruit. What’s not to like?

Commendably serious at the price, the Tin Mine Red is now a blend of Syrah and 28% Mourvèdre, having dispensed with the Grenache. Picked before the rain in 2023, it has appealing white pepper and fennel aromas, lovely granitic intensity, bramble and black cherry flavours and a clean, direct, savoury finish.

Named after the tin mine that was previously located on the farm, this is a newly “premiumised” blend of Chenin Blanc, 24% Chardonnay, 16% Viognier, 8% Roussanne and 7% Semillon from Banghoek and the Polkadraai Hills. Fermented and aged in amphoras and 25% new oak, this a focused, refreshing cuvée with pear, quince and grapefruit flavours and a touch of peachy sweetness.

Purity and focus are the name of the game on this new wine from Hagen Viljoen. Using the 95 and 96 Burgundy clones, it’s a sappy, refreshing, cooler climate style of Chardonnay with a waft of new oak, flavours of pear, lemongrass and cardamom and an undertone of struck match. Mission accomplished.

n: Zevenwacht Z Collection OVP Chenin Blanc
d: The Z Collection Chenin Blanc comes from an old-vine block that was planted in 1981. Picked early for freshness and zip, it uses concrete egg, amphora and new and older oak components for layers of complexity, producing a pithy, racy, lime and green apple palate complemented by a twist of cinnamon spice.

In the past, the Collection Reserve has included a proportion of Petit Verdot from Banghoek, but the 2024 release is a stand-alone Cabernet Sauvignon from a cool site on the Zevenwacht estate. Matured in 60% new oak, it’s firm, youthful and built to age, with aromas of mint, incense and coffee bean and a palate of cassis, mocha and green herbs.

A best-ever Sauvignon Blanc release from Hagen Viljoen, this comes from two blocks planted with the Weather Station and SB11 clones in the highest part of the farm. Combined with 12.5% Semillon, it has 12.5% new oak, as well as a large concrete egg component, layers of nettle, elderflower and pink grapefruit and a flinty finish.

The slopes of the Polkadraai Hills are among the best sites in South Africa to grow Syrah. This comes from a block planted in 1997 and is wonderfully intense and aromatic, with tobacco leaf and allspice notes from 60% whole clusters, layers of bramble, pink grapefruit and tapenade and a firm backbone of sinewy tannins.

This is an unusual Chardonnay from Denzel Swarts, that uses grapes from Paarl with a 20% component from Napier, located to the east of Elim. Tangy, fresh and appealingly restrained, it’s a wine with subtle 20% new oak, pear, clementine and waxed lemon flavours and a focused, refreshing, almost Chablis-esque finish.

Avondale’s biodynamic estate in Paarl supplies the grapes for this Chenin Blanc, which is generally released with a little bottle age. Blended with 5% Semillon, it has negligible oak, flavours of pear, dried honey and baking spices and a racy, well-balanced finish.

n: Zoetendal Vineyards Single Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc
d: Made with fruit from a 1.2-hectare vineyard in Elim, close to the southernmost tip of Africa, this benefits from barrel fermentation in 20% new oak. Wet stone, dill and subtle nutmeg spice aromas are a scented introduction to a palate of pink grapefruit and lime, complemented by a briny sea-breeze finish.

n: Zoetendal Vineyards The Empress Brut CC

d: Vinified at De Grendel until 2023, where Charles Hopkins was the consultant, this is now made at Black Oyster Catcher in Elim, close to the wine’s source in Elim. Very much a cool climate style, with 60% whole bunches, it has top notes of sage, kelp and black pepper, an energetic palate of clove, blackberry and red berries and subtle, older oak integration.

The pick of the current Zonnebloem range, this is sourced from a series of different vineyards in Stellenbosch. Matured in 50% new oak, it has the stony reduction that is often a feature of young Syrah, blackberry, Asian spice and raspberry flavours and a toasty finish.

Banghoek seems to have a natural affinity with Cabernet Franc, given the number of good examples that are produced there. This one is picked in three stages for complexity and nuance, with classic tarragon and graphite aromas, subtle oak, sinewy tannins and a core of cassis, capsicum and black cherry.

Bernard Le Roux sources this Cabernet Sauvignon from two contrasting blocks on the farm, located at different altitudes. Firm, dry and compact, as the estate’s reds tend to be, this has plenty of structure and intensity, damson and blackcurrant pastille flavours and the acidity of a cooler, wetter vintage. One for lovers of traditional red Bordeaux.

Easier to drink that it is to pronounce for a non-Afrikaans speaker, this blend of Merlot, 34% Cabernet Franc and 3% Cabernet Sauvignon is named after a local fynbos shrub. Serious and quite sturdy for a 2023, it has blackberry, dark chocolate and damson flavours, plenty of supporting acidity and a carapace of firm tannins. Impressive at the price.

A stand-alone Petit Verdot has been part of the range at Zorgvliet since 2004, this is something of a speciality, according to Bernard Le Roux. Inky, dense and muscular, as the variety tends to be in its youth, this has plenty of texture, intensity and palate weight, stylish 13% new French oak and layers of fig, plum and damson fruit supported by firm tannins.

Richelle is an ambitious Bordeaux style blend from the lower slopes of the Simonsberg in Banghoek, made from a combination of Cabernet Sauvignon, 17% Petit Verdot, 15% Cabernet Franc and 11% Merlot. Firm, serious and built to last, it’s a wine that will benefit from cellaring, with ample colour, toasty oak, chewy tannins and layers of dark berry fruit.

Simoné is a barrel-fermented white Bordeaux style blend of Sauvignon Blanc and 47% Semillon from the Banghoek Valley, which only sees old wood. Light, pithy and charming, it’s floral and refreshing, with greengage, gooseberry and lemongrass flavours and understated oak spices.

Stefan Johannes has a very clear idea of what he wants to achieve with Zwartwater and I like the direction of travel. This is an engagingly aromatic cuvée of Syrah, 27% Carignan and 5% Mourvèdre, with 73% whole clusters, 20% new oak and a concrete component. Flavours of blackberry, bramble and garrigue spices are supported by a spine of tannin and acidity and subtle reduction.

This is a first release from the historic Lammershoek estate on the Paardeberg, now under new ownership as they say in the hotel trade. It’s a brilliant, layered, complex blend of Chenin Blanc, Viognier, Marsanne and the Hungarian grape Hárslevelű, with aromas of honeysuckle, fennel and wet stone and a tangy, racy palate of orange zest, pear and pink grapefruit. A wine that looks every bit as good as it tastes.
